title: Interlock operational schedule and stakeholder matrix — Q4 2026
body:
Purpose:
This note defines a compact, cross-functional operational schedule and a stakeholder matrix to coordinate the Q4 reliability initiative: the Uptime Interlock Campaign. The doc is intentionally tactical — a working schedule, meeting templates, and the RACI needed to run an SLO-focused rollout across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Use this to align sprint-level work and to hand off to release ops and SRE partners.

Scope and boundaries:
- Scope: onboarding 6 high-priority services to a common SLO baseline (p99 latency and availability SLAs), instrumenting unified telemetry, automated canary verification, and an ops escalation path. Includes product, serving-runtime, infra, observability, and customer-support touchpoints.
- Not in scope: long-term quota model changes, billing pricing adjustments, or deeper model-signature changes.

Primary goals (measurable):
- Baseline coverage: instrumented SLOs for 6 services with guardrails and alerting by week 6.
- Canary success: automated canary test harness passes for each service before rollout to 20% traffic.
- Error budget runway: define acceptable error budget burn policy and automated page triggers; no service exceeds emergency thresholds during rollout.
- Handoff: documented runbooks and a 2-hour knowledge transfer for ops on each service.

High-level timeline (8 weeks) — sprint-aligned:
- Week 0 (Prep): stakeholder kickoff, inventory of services, assign owners, confirm data sources (traces, metrics, logs).
- Week 1–2 (Instrument): implement SLI collection (latency percentiles, success rate), deploy SLO config to sandbox, initial dashboards.
- Week 3 (Validate): smoke tests against sandbox, run synthetic load to simulate tail latency, iterate alerts.
- Week 4 (Canary): publish canary rollout plan, run automated canaries at 5% traffic with rollback automation enabled.
- Week 5 (Scale): expand canary to 20% where safe, monitor error budget and operational noise.
- Week 6 (Full rollout gating): decision gate: metrics, postmortem checklist, runbook readiness. Approve or rollback.
- Week 7–8 (Stabilize + Handoff): finalize runbooks, conduct cross-team retros, and schedule 2-hour ops training sessions per service.

Key milestones and exit criteria:
- Milestone A (Inventory complete): owners assigned and telemetry endpoints validated. Exit: all services report SLIs in observability.
- Milestone B (Canary baseline green): canary tests show <10% extra error budget burn and acceptable p99 shift. Exit: no manual interventions required for 24h.
- Milestone C (Rollout approval): all checklist items passed (runbooks, alerts, rollback tested). Exit: sign-off from product, SRE, and infra leads.

Stakeholder matrix (compact RACI):
- Product (owner: Priya Singh): R: define customer impact and prioritization; A: approve rollout windows; C: accept SLO targets.
- Serving runtime (owner: Daniel Cho): R: implement hooks for latency/KV cache visibility; A: test kernel selection regression risk.
- Observability (owner: Marco Alvarez): R: dashboard templates, alert rules, synthetic canaries; C: provide SLIs and retention plan.
- Platform infra (owner: Ethan Brooks): R: capacity for canaries, autoscaling guardrails; C: approve burst policies.
- SRE / Oncall (owner: Sana Patel): R: runbook authoring, responder for canary incidents; A: escalation authority.
- Customer Success (owner: Kelly O'Neill): C: communicate potential availability windows to customers; I: collect customer impact data post-rollout.

Weekly cadence (standups and deep syncs):
- Monday (15m): Cross-team standup: blockers, data gaps, canary health. Attendees: owners + SRE lead.
- Wednesday (30m): Engineering sync: instrumentation progress, observability, and rollback test status.
- Friday (45m): Readout and gating review when approaching canary or rollout. Includes product, infra, SRE.
- Ad-hoc: War-room template (see below) for any canary > emergency threshold.

Meeting templates (short):
- Kickoff agenda: goals, scope, owners, risk review, immediate actions, comms channel, success criteria.
- Canary readout template: metrics observed (p50/p95/p99 shift), error budget burn, traces (examples), human interventions, decision (advance/pause/rollback).

War-room (ad-hoc) playbook steps:
1) Triage: capture timeline, metric changes, and recent deploys.
2) Containment: activate rollback automation if canary policy triggers.
3) Communication: update #uptime-interlock with incident summary and ETA.
4) Postmortem: 72h follow-up with owner and SRE.

Risk register (top risks and mitigations):
- Risk: Alerts spam during canary. Mitigation: mute non-critical groups and route to a temporary canary channel.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps prevent gating. Mitigation: fallback synthetic tests + manual smoke run.
- Risk: Insufficient capacity for synthetic load. Mitigation: reserve burst pool in infra for test windows.

Dependencies and lanes (quick):
- Observability: dashboards and retention config — must complete by end of Week 2.
- Infra: reserve capacity + autoscaler policy — must complete by Week 3.
- Serving runtime: low-level kernel/quantization check — must be validated by Week 3.
- Customer comms: templated notice ready by Week 4 for any canary impacting customers.

Acceptance criteria for a single service rollout:
- SLIs are collected and validated in staging for 72h.
- Canary automation executes and can rollback without human interference in test mode.
- Ops runbook (one pager) is published and tested in tabletop.
- Product + SRE sign-off recorded in the gating doc.

Communication plan & escalation contact list:
- Primary channel: #uptime-interlock (Slack). Secondary: incident bridge.
- Pager: SRE on-call (Sana Patel). Backup pager: Platform lead (Ethan Brooks).
- Exec digest: weekly summary to VP Eng and Head of Product on Fridays if there are gating events.

Artifacts to produce (deliverables):
- SLO config JSON for each service (checked into ops repo).
- Readout dashboard link and synthetic test harness runbook.
- One-page service runbook per service.
- Postmortem template and retro notes.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- Priya: finalize prioritized service list by 2026-09-14.
- Daniel: validate telemetry hooks on service A+B by 2026-09-18.
- Marco: create dashboard template and shared folder by 2026-09-20.
- Ethan: reserve burst capacity windows (two 3-hour windows) by 2026-09-22.
- Sana: draft war-room checklist and runbook skeleton by 2026-09-24.

How to use this doc:
- Treat this as the canonical short-term operational schedule. Edit in place when gates pass or timelines shift. When the rollout completes, we will extract runbooks into the ops-runbooks repo and move the finalized artifacts to Confluence.

Notes and open questions:
- Can we standardize a rollback signal across the serving runtime variants? (action: Daniel + Marco investigate by 2026-09-17)
- Do we need a leased GPU pool for synthetic latency tests to avoid noisy-neighbor effects? (action: Ethan to cost and reserve options)

Version history:
- 2026-09-10: initial draft — Ava
- 2026-09-18: added milestone gating and canary template — Daniel
- 2026-10-02: updated dependencies and immediate action dates — Ava
